work.title: Find a better explanation. Choose a practical response.
work.summary: Start with a recurring delivery or operating problem, or a decision where the usual answers are not helping. I work with you to examine the evidence, explore overlooked connections and decide what to do next.
work.fitTitle: Where I can be most useful
work.fit: Recurring operating problems. Busy teams making slow progress. Gaps between customer promises and execution. Decisions about technology, learning or change that need a clearer rationale.
work.fitClosing: My experience spans engineering, delivery, commercial responsibility, capability building and running a business. The first discussion establishes how that experience can help with your particular challenge.
work.agreement: The problem and intended outcome; people involved; evidence to review; deliverables; schedule; fee; and each person’s responsibilities. If the work needs a different specialist, I will say so.
work.boundary: You receive advice and agreed support grounded in the available evidence. Business outcomes also depend on the decisions made, implementation and conditions outside the engagement.
work.healthSummary: The Business and Delivery Health Check is a diagnostic review of one delivery area, with findings and a prioritised 90-day action plan.

sprint.title: Problem-Solving Sprint
sprint.tagline: Look beyond the first explanation. Decide what to do next.
sprint.summary: Work directly with me to examine one recurring problem or difficult decision. We test the initial explanation, look for overlooked causes and turn the findings into a practical next move.
sprint.fit: A problem keeps returning; the team has competing explanations; a proposed solution needs testing; or the available information is not producing a clear decision.
sprint.deliverables: A problem brief describing the situation, intended outcome and constraints. A decision note setting out the evidence, assumptions, options and recommended direction. A 30-day action plan with agreed owners, first steps and review measures. A readout to discuss the findings and decisions.
sprint.process: We agree the question, intended outcome and boundaries. You bring the context and access to agreed participants and materials. I examine the evidence, look across the technical, commercial and operating factors, and test competing explanations. We discuss the options and finish with an action plan and a scheduled review of the first steps.
sprint.scope: The Sprint covers one challenge and an agreed set of participants and materials. The proposal confirms the timetable, evidence required, fee and review date. Implementation beyond the agreed review is scoped separately.
sprint.exclusionsTitle: What the Sprint does not include
sprint.exclusions: An open-ended organisational review, outsourced delivery, technical certification or a guaranteed business result. Where the next step needs a specialist, that requirement will be made clear.
sprint.closing: Discuss the problem before choosing the engagement.

implementation.title: Help the agreed change take hold
implementation.summary: A recommendation becomes useful when someone can act on it. I help turn an agreed decision into a defined piece of work with clear ownership, review points and a practical handover.
implementation.examples: Simplifying a reporting process. Clarifying a sales-to-delivery handover. Establishing a decision and review routine. Piloting a capability programme. Helping a team evaluate a technology use case.
implementation.agreement: A specific work package, outputs, responsibilities, time commitment and completion criteria. Your team retains responsibility for operating decisions and ongoing delivery. I take responsibility for the advisory, facilitation and artefacts explicitly included in the engagement.
implementation.deliverables: An agreed work plan, the documents or working practices defined in scope, progress reviews and a handover note identifying what is complete and what still needs attention.
implementation.boundary: This is scoped support, not an unlimited delivery commitment. It can follow a Sprint or begin from an existing decision that is clear enough to implement.

workshop.title: Understand the issue together. Practise a useful response.
workshop.summary: A focused workshop helps a team work through a real challenge and leave with a shared understanding and practical actions.
workshop.themes: Framing the right problem. Making complex ideas understandable. Improving decisions and ownership. Connecting learning to work. Examining an AI use case before committing to it.
workshop.deliverables: A discovery discussion, a tailored agenda, facilitated exercises using an agreed example, and a short action summary. The proposal confirms participants, session format, duration and follow-up.
workshop.boundary: Workshops use approved examples and material. They do not require participants to share confidential information in public tools.

about.title: I look for what the usual explanation leaves out.
about.summary: I am Sriram Srinivasan, founder of Sriram Advisory. My 30-year background connects software engineering at Polaris, delivery and practice leadership at Wipro, pre-sales, entrepreneurship and AI enablement.
about.connections: These areas influence one another. A delivery problem can begin with an unclear promise. A learning problem can begin with the way work is assigned. A technology decision can become easier when the business question is made more precise.
about.approach: I look across technical, commercial and operating perspectives, ask what has been overlooked and test alternative explanations against the evidence. The aim is a useful decision and a practical way to learn from what happens next.
about.process: I explain the reasoning behind a recommendation. I distinguish evidence from assumptions. I make the scope and responsibilities explicit. I help with the agreed next steps and review what changes.
about.spanforge: Alongside Sriram Advisory, I am developing Spanforge, focused on testing and security tools for AI agents.

situations: The same delivery issue keeps returning.
The fixes help briefly. You need to understand what keeps recreating the problem.
Everyone is busy, but progress is slow.
You need to see where effort goes and what prevents work from moving.
Before investing in training, tools or AI, you want to test whether it addresses the actual constraint.
exampleStages: “Our team is missing commitments. We need productivity training.”
How many tasks are active, where work waits, how priorities change and how much work must be repeated.
The team may know how to do the work but lack enough uninterrupted time and timely decisions.
Limit concurrent work for one team, assign an owner to blocked decisions and review progress weekly.
Shorter completion times, fewer blocked items and less rework, without shifting the burden elsewhere.

faq: Do I need to know exactly what the problem is?
No. Describe what is happening and what you want to improve. The first discussion helps establish the question and whether I can be useful.

Business owners, leaders and teams facing recurring problems or difficult decisions. My background includes technology, enterprise delivery, commercial work and entrepreneurship. We begin by checking whether that experience fits your challenge.
Will you help us implement the recommendation?

Yes, where the work fits my experience and we agree a defined scope. Implementation support is a separate commitment with clear outputs and responsibilities. It is not automatically included in a diagnostic review.
How are fees and timing agreed?
The proposal confirms the work, deliverables, schedule and fee before the engagement begins. Sending an enquiry does not commit you to a paid service.

AI may help organise agreed information and explore possible interpretations. I review the evidence and take responsibility for the advice. Any use of client material is agreed in advance; sensitive material is not entered into public AI tools by default.
A short description of the situation is enough. Please do not send confidential files or personal records with the initial enquiry. We can agree what evidence is needed later.
I commit to the agreed work and deliverables. Business outcomes also depend on implementation, decisions and conditions outside the engagement.
